title: Par Class
summary: Official Derivative Python API reference for a single parameter object, covering constant values, expressions, bind/export metadata, menus, parameter modes, custom-parameter attributes, evaluation methods, pulse/reset/copy/destroy behavior, and parameter identity.
guidance: Use this article when generated Python needs to read, write, pulse, or inspect a specific parameter.
Set val for the constant-mode value only; use eval() for the current working value across constant, expression, export, and bind modes.
Setting expr or mode changes parameter evaluation state, so transaction validators should check intended mode changes explicitly.
For menu parameters, prefer menuNames/menuLabels for definitions and menuIndex when the target value is a numeric menu choice.
Use evalOPs() for OP parameters that can resolve multiple operators, because plain eval() may return one OP, a list, or None depending on matches.
Only custom and sequential parameters can be destroyed, and existing parameter objects should be re-fetched after destruction.
